```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(bigIRT)
```

A large fit is expensive, and the questions asked of it afterwards are many:
does this item behave differently for girls and boys, does that one drift
with age, does school type predict ability once the rest is accounted for?
Refitting for each question does not scale. Score-based tests answer them
from one fit: each person's contribution to the score of the marginal
likelihood says which way, and how strongly, that person's responses pull on
every parameter, and a covariate that orders those pulls is evidence that the
parameter depends on it.

`scoreContributions()` computes the contributions, and `scoreTest()` turns
them into tests: parametric score (LM) tests with a one-step estimate of the
effect, and nonparametric fluctuation tests that need no functional form.

## Data with impact and DIF

The covariate `z` raises ability (impact), and makes items 1 to 4 easier
for persons with high `z` (uniform DIF).

```{r data}
set.seed(1)
N <- 1500; J <- 20
a <- rlnorm(J, 0, .2); b <- rnorm(J)
z <- runif(N)
theta <- rnorm(N) + (z > .5)
B <- matrix(b, N, J, byrow = TRUE)
B[, 1:4] <- B[, 1:4] - 1.2 * (z - .5)
P <- plogis(matrix(a, N, J, byrow = TRUE) * theta - B)
dat <- data.frame(id = rep(1:N, J), Item = rep(1:J, each = N), Scale = 1,
  score = rbinom(N * J, 1, P))
dat$z <- z[dat$id]
```

## The covariate belongs in the ability model

Score contributions have mean zero, for every person and conditionally on
the person's covariates, when the model is right. A covariate that is
related to ability is therefore part of the model: left out, its effect on
ability shows up as DIF in every item. So it goes into `personPreds`, in a
form flexible enough to carry the relation -- here a spline, since the
impact is a step that a linear term would not capture.

```{r fit}
Bz <- splines::ns(z, df = 3)
dat[c("z1", "z2", "z3")] <- Bz[dat$id, ]
fit <- fitIRT(dat, pl = 2, personPreds = c("z1", "z2", "z3"),
  laplaceRefine = "agq", cores = 2, verbose = 0)
```

`laplaceRefine = "agq"` finishes the fit on the quadrature marginal, the
same one the score contributions are computed from, so their sums vanish at
the estimates. It matters most when each person answers few items.

## DIF: one test per item

```{r dif}
sc <- scoreContributions(fit)
cov <- data.frame(id = rownames(fit$pars$Ability))
cov$z <- z[as.integer(cov$id)]
dif <- scoreTest(sc, cov, parameters = "B", form = "linear")
dif
```

The `coefficients` are one-step estimates of each item's linear DIF slope on
the intercept scale (positive is harder), with standard errors: what a refit
with `BitemPreds = "z"` and `itemSpecificBetas = TRUE` would estimate.

```{r epc}
head(dif$coefficients[order(item)], 6)
```

Uniform DIF that every item shares cannot be told apart from an effect on
ability, and the ability model absorbs it; DIF is measured relative to it.

The same contributions test non-uniform DIF (`parameters = "A"`), both
jointly (`c("B", "A")`), the asymptotes of a 3PL or 4PL (`"C"`, `"D"`), and
other functional forms: `form = "spline"` for smooth nonlinear relations,
`"factor"` for groups, and `"fluctuation"` for the nonparametric double-max,
Cramer-von Mises and maxLM tests, whose p-values are simulated from the
process's exact covariance (so they hold even though, with impact,
information does not accrue evenly along `z`).

```{r fluct}
fl <- scoreTest(sc, cov, parameters = "B", form = "fluctuation", items = 1:6, seed = 1)
fl$tests[, .(item, DM, p_DM, p_CvM, p_maxLM)]
```

## Covariates of ability

`parameters = "Ability"` asks whether a covariate predicts ability beyond
what the ability model already holds. `w` here is noise, and `z` is already
in the model through its spline, so neither should be flagged.

```{r ability}
cov$w <- rnorm(nrow(cov))
scoreTest(sc, cov[c("id", "w")], parameters = "Ability")$tests
```

## Covariates that vary within person

Covariates can also be given per response -- one row per row of the data
passed to `fitIRT()` -- for example age at the time of each response, or the
item's position in the test. Then `by = "all"` tests one coefficient shared by
every item, and a vector of item groups tests one per group.

```{r rows}
pos <- ave(dat$id, dat$id, FUN = function(x) sample(seq_along(x)))
scoreTest(sc, data.frame(position = pos), parameters = "B", by = "all")$tests
```
